description: SMARTS definitions for functional groups recognised by synth-path-helper. The first atom of each pattern is the 'anchor' atom used to count distinct occurrences.

groups.name: Primary alcohol
groups.notes: R-CH2-OH. Oxidised to an aldehyde (PCC, DMP, Swern) or to a carboxylic acid (Jones, KMnO4).

groups.name: Secondary alcohol
groups.notes: R2CH-OH. Oxidised to a ketone; cannot be oxidised further without C-C cleavage.

groups.name: Tertiary alcohol
groups.notes: R3C-OH. No alpha-H, so not oxidised by PCC or Jones. Readily undergoes SN1 and E1 via a tertiary carbocation.

groups.name: Phenol
groups.notes: Ar-OH. pKa ~10; strongly activating ortho/para director in EAS.

groups.name: Aldehyde
groups.notes: R-CHO. Reduced by NaBH4 to a primary alcohol; easily oxidised to a carboxylic acid.

groups.name: Ketone
groups.notes: R2C=O. Reduced by NaBH4 to a secondary alcohol; resistant to mild oxidants.

groups.name: Carboxylic acid
groups.notes: R-COOH. pKa ~4-5. Reduced only by strong hydride donors (LiAlH4, BH3).

groups.name: Ester
groups.notes: R-COOR'. Hydrolysed by NaOH (saponification); reduced by LiAlH4 but not by NaBH4.

groups.name: Amide
groups.notes: R-CONR'2. Least reactive acid derivative; hydrolysis needs strong acid or base and heat.

groups.name: Acyl halide
groups.notes: R-COCl. Most reactive acid derivative; reacts with water, alcohols and amines.

groups.name: Acid anhydride
groups.notes: (RCO)2O. Acylating agent, a little milder than acyl chlorides.

groups.name: Nitrile
groups.notes: R-C#N. Hydrolysed to a carboxylic acid; reduced by LiAlH4 to a primary amine.

groups.name: Alkene
groups.notes: C=C. Nucleophilic pi bond; electrophilic additions follow Markovnikov's rule unless the mechanism is radical or concerted (hydroboration).

groups.name: Alkyne
groups.notes: C#C. Can be reduced to a cis-alkene (Lindlar), a trans-alkene (Na/NH3) or an alkane (H2, Pd/C).

groups.name: Terminal alkyne
groups.notes: R-C#C-H. The sp C-H is acidic (pKa ~25), so NaNH2 makes an acetylide nucleophile.

groups.name: Benzene ring
groups.notes: Aromatic ring. Undergoes electrophilic aromatic substitution (EAS); existing substituents set the regiochemistry.

groups.name: Primary (or methyl) alkyl halide
groups.notes: R-CH2-X. Good SN2 substrate; with bulky bases E2 can compete.

groups.name: Secondary alkyl halide
groups.notes: R2CH-X. SN2 and E2 compete; strong, basic nucleophiles favour E2.

groups.name: Tertiary alkyl halide
groups.notes: R3C-X. No SN2. E2 with strong base; SN1/E1 in polar protic solvents.

groups.name: Aryl halide
groups.notes: Ar-X. Inert to SN1/SN2; forms Grignard reagents (Br, I) and couples under Pd catalysis.

groups.name: Grignard reagent
groups.notes: R-MgX. Strong carbon nucleophile and base; destroyed by water and alcohols.

groups.name: Primary aliphatic amine
groups.notes: R-NH2. Basic (pKaH ~10) and nucleophilic.

groups.name: Secondary aliphatic amine
groups.notes: R2NH. Basic and nucleophilic.

groups.name: Tertiary aliphatic amine
groups.notes: R3N. Base; cannot be acylated.

groups.name: Aromatic amine (aniline)
groups.notes: Ar-NH2. Strong ortho/para activator. Ar-NH2 forms diazonium salts (NaNO2, HCl) for Sandmeyer chemistry.

groups.name: Nitro group
groups.notes: R-NO2. Strong meta-directing deactivator; reduced to an amine (Sn/HCl, Fe/HCl, H2/Pd).

groups.name: Ether
groups.notes: R-O-R'. Fairly unreactive; common solvents (Et2O, THF). Cleaved by HI or HBr.

groups.name: Epoxide
groups.notes: Strained three-membered cyclic ether. Opened by nucleophiles: at the less hindered carbon under basic conditions, at the more substituted carbon under acidic conditions.

groups.name: Thiol
groups.notes: R-SH. More acidic and nucleophilic than alcohols; oxidised easily to disulfides.
